articles.title: Anthropic 如何在 Claude 写下 Claude Code 约 90% 代码后重新设计代码评审
articles.summary: 作者解读 Anthropic 关于 Claude Code 代码评审重构的博客：Claude 写了约 90% 的代码，2026 年 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上而 revert 率下降超 40%。
articles.content:
当 Claude 写了 Claude Code 约 90% 的代码后，团队如何重新设计代码评审 ？

Anthropic 没有取消代码评审，是把 “人读代码” 这个动作大部分交给了机器，把稀缺的人类注意力只花在真正需要判断力的地方。核心转变是：从“这段代码有人看过吗”变成“这个变更可能出什么问题，哪种检查（自动或人工）最适合抓住它”。

claude.dev/blog/solving-c…

# 为什么必须改？

背景数字：2026 年 6 月到 9 月，合并的 PR 数量翻倍以上，而 revert 率下降超 40%。传统的“同事互相读 diff”模式在这个吞吐量下会先崩溃；人要么变成瓶颈，要么敷衍放行。

团队对成本的认识很清醒：人力时间 = 评审时间 + 修复坏代码的时间，压缩一头只会把成本转移到另一头。所以他们不追踪“评审覆盖率”这种虚荣指标，而转去追踪 “每个 PR 平均几个人类审批” 和 “等人审批的等待时间”，并以 revert 率 / 事故率作为护栏指标；目标是最多一个人在环（有时只有作者本人），且事故不比以前多。

# 七层防线：一个变更的一生

1. PR 之前的自我验证 — Claude 必须出示证据（测试输出、构建、截图）而不是声称完成；再用一个全新上下文的第二个 agent 审 diff。Boris Cherny（Claude Code 创造者）认为给 Claude 一个验证方法是“最重要的事”，效果提升 2–3 倍。反复出现的问题会被固化到源头：写进 CLAUDE.md（项目约定）和 REVIEW.md（给代码主人看的指引——失败长什么样、nit 上限、哪些路径跳过，且每条发现必须附文件/行号证据）。

2. 每个 PR 必过 AI 评审 — 内部 PR 上“实质性评审意见”占比从 16% 升到 54%；千行以上的大 PR 几乎总能查出问题。多个 agent 并行找 bug，再有 verifier agent 对每条发现投票才发出。发现分为 Important / Nit / Pre-existing，每条必须解决或说明理由。

3. 阻塞性的安全评审 — 独立的自动化通道，有未处理发现就不能合并。

4. 阻塞性的自动检查 — lint、类型、跨平台测试、构建；PR 模板强制填写“如何测试的”和“如何回滚”，且需一人签字。

5. 基于风险的人工审批 — 分类器定级：低风险（文档、文案）不需人工；中风险（普通产品变更，及缓存、自动更新器、系统提示词等敏感区）一人；高风险两人。关键规则：agent 的批准永远不能算人工批准；批准只覆盖一个 commit，有新提交就要重新审批。

6. 合并队列 + 特性开关 + 灰度 — 针对合并后 main 重跑检查；新行为先给 Anthropic 内部员工，再走 latest channel，最后进 stable。

7. 快速检测与回滚 — 开关无需重新部署即可关闭；事故复盘必问“哪一层本该拦住它”。

# 两个最有参考价值的工程细节

1. 评审器本身也是被持续评测的系统。 过去引发事故的 PR（经专家确认）构成一个 eval 集，评审器每天跑分，只有分数提升的改动才被保留；噪声则通过“人对评论的反应”和“在已知干净的 PR 上跑评审器”来度量。这本质上是把“评审质量”从主观感受变成了可优化的目标函数。

2. 收敛问题的解法。 曾有一个 agent 写的 CLI PR 一夜跑了 50+ 轮评审，而 git blame 显示约 59% 被标记的代码在第一轮之前就存在；评审 agent 在翻旧账而不是审新变更。修复手段：三轮封顶（超过就退回来重新考虑方案）、后续轮次只看增量 diff、标记 bug 类别而非单行、禁止重复发现。效果：一轮通过率 65%→78%，5 轮以上 PR 从 8.9% 降到 1.5%，平均评审轮次 2.08→1.32。这是 AI 评审 AI 代码时特有的“死循环”问题，他们的解法值得所有引入 AI reviewer 的团队抄作业。

# 人类还留在哪里？

· 该不该做：方向、品味、范围；

· 高危代码：计费、自动更新器、CI 工作流；

· 可被复制模仿的架构决策；

· 读证据：测试输出、截图、发现列表；

· 为结果负责：每个上线变更背后必须有一个承担问责的人。

Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code.

From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled while the share reverted fell by more than 40%.

We wrote about how we changed code review to get there, and how to adopt it:

claude.dev/blog/solving-c…

articles.title: Muse Spark Open (Max) 登顶 Code Arena: WebDev 美国开源模型第一
articles.summary: Arena 公布 Meta 发布的 Muse Spark Open (Max) 在 Code Arena: WebDev 以 1511 分位居美国开源模型第一、开源模型总榜第 13。
articles.content:
Exciting news: Muse Spark Open (Max) by @AIatMeta is the #1 US open model in the Code Arena: WebDev! With 1511 pts, it’s #13 among open models overall.

As the first open-weight release in the Muse Spark family, it scored 156 pts above Muse Glimmer, @AIatMeta’s earlier open model at #41 among open models with 1355 pts.

Priced at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M input/output tokens, it’s 79% less than Muse Wonder (Max) and priced on par with Muse Spark 1.3 (Max).

By domain, Muse Spark Open (Max) ranks:

- #13 in Brand & Marketing, and in Data & Analytics

- #14 in Reference-Based Design

- #15 Gaming, and in Consumer Product

- #20 in Simulations

Congrats to the team at @AIatMeta on this contribution to the open ecosystem!

Today we’re releasing Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date.

Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

Key Model Specs:

→ 816B total / 42B active parameters

→ 1M token
articles.author: X：Arena (@arena)
articles.recommendation: 基于 Arena 自家 Code Arena 榜单给出 Muse Spark Open 的具体得分、排名与定价对比，读者可据此定位该开源模型的真实水准。

articles.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 发布，多基准成绩提升且 API 价格不变
articles.summary: DeepSeek 将 V4.1 Flash 升级至 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017，网页端与 APP 同步更新，API 调用方式与价格不变，仍用 deepseek-flash 访问。
articles.content:
更新日志

时间: 2026-10-17

开放自研搜索 API

DeepSeek 网页端与 API 端的搜索能力均由自研 DeepSeek 搜索引擎提供底层支持，稳定处理每天来自全球各地的数亿次搜索请求。DeepSeek 搜索是 AI 原生的通用搜索引擎，索引了全球千亿级网页，支持多语言搜索，实时返回高相关、高权威、高时效的优质结果。针对 SEO 作弊、GEO 操纵和低质 AIGC，我们通过严格的识别机制进行过滤，确保向用户与 LLM 呈现权威可信的信息。使用方式请参考网页搜索与抓取指南。

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 更新

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 已升级至 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017，官方网页端与 APP 模型也已同步更新至新版本。API 调用方式与价格保持不变，仍使用 deepseek-flash 即可访问最新模型。

相比上一版本的 DeepSeek V4.1，新模型在各基准测试中取得了显著提升：

- HLE (w/o tools): 42.6 (44.0*)

- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 42.3

- DeepSWE v1.1: 77.0

- ProgramBench: 29.1

- NL2Repo-Bench: 68.2

- Automation-Bench v1.0.6: 60.5

- Agents' Last Exam: 35.4

- Apex Bench v1.1: 72.1

- Chartography (w/tools): 83.0

- BabyVision (w/tools): 92.5

- ZeroBench-main (w/tools): 51.0

* 表示仅在 HLE 评测集的纯文本子集上进行了测试；Terminal-Bench 4.0 使用 Claude Code 框架测试，DeepSWE 使用 Mini-SWE-V2 框架测试；ZeroBench-main 使用 Pass@5 评测。

在提升性能的同时，我们还缩短了模型的任务运行时间与输出长度，让用户能够以更低成本、更快速度完成任务，在多个 Harness 下达到新的性能-费用帕累托最优。我们特别针对 DeepSeek Harness、腾讯 CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy 等平台框架进行了优化。请升级至 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.1 及以上版本，以获得适配新版模型的最佳体验。

时间: 2026-09-10

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 发布

今天，我们正式发布 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 模型。这是我们全新模型结构系列中的最小尺寸的模型，具备原生多模态视觉理解能力。新模型结构的设计初衷是：能力上限更高、推理速度更快、吞吐更大、可扩展到更大参数模型。

- GPQA Diamond: 90.9

- HLE: 36.8 (39.1*)

- Codeforces (Rating): 3471

- MathArena Apex: 65.6

- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 90.6

- Terminal-Bench 3.0: 30.0

- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 31.2

- DeepSWE v1.1: 74.2

- ProgramBench: 20.3

- NL2Repo-Bench: 65.4

- CyberGym: 88.1

- SEC-Bench Pro: 62.8

- ExploitGym: 15.3

- HLE (w/tools): 63.9

- Automation-Bench: 54.8

- Agents' Last Exam: 31.8

- Chartography (w/tools): 78.9

- BabyVision (w/tools): 89.6

- ZeroBench-main (w/tools): 49.0

* 表示仅在 HLE 评测集的纯文本子集上进行了测试。

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 已同步上线 DeepSeek API，原生支持多模态，将模型名称更改为 deepseek-flash 即可调用最新的 V4.1 Flash 模型。旧版本模型 V4 Flash 与 V4 Flash Vision Exp 现已下线，出于兼容考虑，模型名 deepseek-v4-flash、deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp 将被暂时路由到 V4.1 Flash。

为响应广大用户的需求，我们决定在 2026 年 9 月 14 日之后继续提供 DeepSeek V4 Pro 的 API 调用服务，计费方式保持不变；如有变动，我们将另行通知。感谢您的理解与支持！

API 定价调整

随着 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 上线，API 价格同步下调。详细价格请参考模型与价格。

详细更新内容请参阅文档。

时间: 2026-08-21

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 发布

今天，全新的多模态视觉理解模型 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 上线 DeepSeek API 平台，这是一个实验性质的模型，用户可以通过设置 model='deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp' 访问该模型。

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 83.9

- NL2Repo: 57.7

- DeepSWE: 59.3

- DSBench-Hard: 63.6

- AutomationBench (Public): 25.7

- ApexBench (Pass@1): 36.5

- Agents' Last Exam: 27.3

- Chartography: 64.3

- ZeroBench (Pass@5): 35.0

* 对于公开基准测试集中的 Code Agent 文本任务，DeepSeek 系列模型使用 DeepSeek Harness 极简模式作为框架进行测试，并使用 max 档位，topp=0.95，temperature=1.0；在 ApexBench 与 Agents' Last Exam 测评中，文本模型 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 会忽略其中的多模态元素

在纯文本能力（Agent、推理、世界知识等）方面，DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 与 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 正式版持平。

在需要视觉理解的 Agent Benchmark 上，DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 相比 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 实现了大幅跃升，多模态 Agent 能力已接近 Opus-4.8。

详细调用方法请参阅文档。

时间: 2026-08-13

DeepSeek-V4-Pro 更新

DeepSeek-V4-Pro 正式版已同步在 APP、网页端和 API 更新上线。API 调用方式不变，模型名设置为 deepseek-v4-pro，即可使用最新版本。

正式版 DeepSeek V4 Pro 极大增强了 Agent 能力，在生产环境中的性能表现提升尤为显著。

- HLE (wo / w tools): 42.7/60.0

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 87.9

- NL2Repo: 61.5

- Cybergym: 83.3

- DeepSWE: 62.7

- Toolathlon-Verified: 74.1

- Agents' Last Exam: 25.7

- AutomationBench (Public): 31.8

- DSBench-FullStack: 71.1

- DSBench-Hard: 67.2

原生支持 Responses API

DeepSeek API 现已原生支持 OpenAI Responses API 格式，并针对性适配 Codex。用户可以参考官方文档，通过一键配置脚本完成 Codex 的配置。

更灵活的思考强度控制

V4-Pro 和 V4-Flash 思考模式现支持 low / high / max 三档思考强度，用户在实际使用中可以根据任务复杂度灵活选择：简单任务使用 low，日常 Agent 任务使用 high，更复杂的任务场景使用 max。设置方法请参考官方 API 文档：思考模式。

API 定价调整

随着 DeepSeek V4 全系列模型正式版上线，我们将对 API 价格进行更新调整。为了更加合理地调配资源，我们将采用峰谷定价，闲时价格为高峰时段价格的一半，鼓励用户根据实际使用情况调整任务时间。新价格将于北京时间 2026 年 8 月 17 日 0 时开始生效。

详细更新内容请参阅文档

时间: 2026-07-31

DeepSeek-V4-Flash 更新

DeepSeek-V4-Flash 正式版 API 上线公测，API 调用方式不变，模型名设置为 deepseek-v4-flash 即可使用最新版本。

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 82.7

- NL2Repo: 54.2

- Cybergym: 76.7

- DeepSWE: 54.4

- Toolathlon verified: 70.3

- Agent Last Exam: 25.2

- Automation Bench (Public): 25.1

- DSBench-FullStack: 68.7

- DSBench-Hard: 59.6

articles.content:
更新日志

时间: 2026-10-17

开放自研搜索 API

DeepSeek 网页端与 API 端的搜索能力均由自研 DeepSeek 搜索引擎提供底层支持，稳定处理每天来自全球各地的数亿次搜索请求。DeepSeek 搜索是 AI 原生的通用搜索引擎，索引了全球千亿级网页，支持多语言搜索，实时返回高相关、高权威、高时效的优质结果。针对 SEO 作弊、GEO 操纵和低质 AIGC，我们通过严格的识别机制进行过滤，确保向用户与 LLM 呈现权威可信的信息。使用方式请参考网页搜索与抓取指南。

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 更新

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 已升级至 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017，官方网页端与 APP 模型也已同步更新至新版本。API 调用方式与价格保持不变，仍使用 deepseek-flash 即可访问最新模型。

相比上一版本的 DeepSeek V4.1，新模型在各基准测试中取得了显著提升：

- HLE (w/o tools): 42.6 (44.0*)

- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 42.3

- DeepSWE v1.1: 77.0

- ProgramBench: 29.1

- NL2Repo-Bench: 68.2

- Automation-Bench v1.0.6: 60.5

- Agents' Last Exam: 35.4

- Apex Bench v1.1: 72.1

- Chartography (w/tools): 83.0

- BabyVision (w/tools): 92.5

- ZeroBench-main (w/tools): 51.0

* 表示仅在 HLE 评测集的纯文本子集上进行了测试；Terminal-Bench 4.0 使用 Claude Code 框架测试，DeepSWE 使用 Mini-SWE-V2 框架测试；ZeroBench-main 使用 Pass@5 评测。

在提升性能的同时，我们还缩短了模型的任务运行时间与输出长度，让用户能够以更低成本、更快速度完成任务，在多个 Harness 下达到新的性能-费用帕累托最优。我们特别针对 DeepSeek Harness、腾讯 CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy 等平台框架进行了优化。请升级至 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.1 及以上版本，以获得适配新版模型的最佳体验。

时间: 2026-09-10

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 发布

今天，我们正式发布 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 模型。这是我们全新模型结构系列中的最小尺寸的模型，具备原生多模态视觉理解能力。新模型结构的设计初衷是：能力上限更高、推理速度更快、吞吐更大、可扩展到更大参数模型。

- GPQA Diamond: 90.9

- HLE: 36.8 (39.1*)

- Codeforces (Rating): 3471

- MathArena Apex: 65.6

- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 90.6

- Terminal-Bench 3.0: 30.0

- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 31.2

- DeepSWE v1.1: 74.2

- ProgramBench: 20.3

- NL2Repo-Bench: 65.4

- CyberGym: 88.1

- SEC-Bench Pro: 62.8

- ExploitGym: 15.3

- HLE (w/tools): 63.9

- Automation-Bench: 54.8

- Agents' Last Exam: 31.8

- Chartography (w/tools): 78.9

- BabyVision (w/tools): 89.6

- ZeroBench-main (w/tools): 49.0

* 表示仅在 HLE 评测集的纯文本子集上进行了测试。

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 已同步上线 DeepSeek API，原生支持多模态，将模型名称更改为 deepseek-flash 即可调用最新的 V4.1 Flash 模型。旧版本模型 V4 Flash 与 V4 Flash Vision Exp 现已下线，出于兼容考虑，模型名 deepseek-v4-flash、deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp 将被暂时路由到 V4.1 Flash。

为响应广大用户的需求，我们决定在 2026 年 9 月 14 日之后继续提供 DeepSeek V4 Pro 的 API 调用服务，计费方式保持不变；如有变动，我们将另行通知。感谢您的理解与支持！

API 定价调整

随着 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 上线，API 价格同步下调。详细价格请参考模型与价格。

详细更新内容请参阅文档。

时间: 2026-08-21

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 发布

今天，全新的多模态视觉理解模型 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 上线 DeepSeek API 平台，这是一个实验性质的模型，用户可以通过设置 model='deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp' 访问该模型。

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 83.9

- NL2Repo: 57.7

- DeepSWE: 59.3

- DSBench-Hard: 63.6

- AutomationBench (Public): 25.7

- ApexBench (Pass@1): 36.5

- Agents' Last Exam: 27.3

- Chartography: 64.3

- ZeroBench (Pass@5): 35.0

* 对于公开基准测试集中的 Code Agent 文本任务，DeepSeek 系列模型使用 DeepSeek Harness 极简模式作为框架进行测试，并使用 max 档位，topp=0.95，temperature=1.0；在 ApexBench 与 Agents' Last Exam 测评中，文本模型 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 会忽略其中的多模态元素

在纯文本能力（Agent、推理、世界知识等）方面，DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 与 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 正式版持平。

在需要视觉理解的 Agent Benchmark 上，DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 相比 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 实现了大幅跃升，多模态 Agent 能力已接近 Opus-4.8。

详细调用方法请参阅文档。

时间: 2026-08-13

DeepSeek-V4-Pro 更新

DeepSeek-V4-Pro 正式版已同步在 APP、网页端和 API 更新上线。API 调用方式不变，模型名设置为 deepseek-v4-pro，即可使用最新版本。

正式版 DeepSeek V4 Pro 极大增强了 Agent 能力，在生产环境中的性能表现提升尤为显著。

- HLE (wo / w tools): 42.7/60.0

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 87.9

- NL2Repo: 61.5

- Cybergym: 83.3

- DeepSWE: 62.7

- Toolathlon-Verified: 74.1

- Agents' Last Exam: 25.7

- AutomationBench (Public): 31.8

- DSBench-FullStack: 71.1

- DSBench-Hard: 67.2

原生支持 Responses API

DeepSeek API 现已原生支持 OpenAI Responses API 格式，并针对性适配 Codex。用户可以参考官方文档，通过一键配置脚本完成 Codex 的配置。

更灵活的思考强度控制

V4-Pro 和 V4-Flash 思考模式现支持 low / high / max 三档思考强度，用户在实际使用中可以根据任务复杂度灵活选择：简单任务使用 low，日常 Agent 任务使用 high，更复杂的任务场景使用 max。设置方法请参考官方 API 文档：思考模式。

API 定价调整

随着 DeepSeek V4 全系列模型正式版上线，我们将对 API 价格进行更新调整。为了更加合理地调配资源，我们将采用峰谷定价，闲时价格为高峰时段价格的一半，鼓励用户根据实际使用情况调整任务时间。新价格将于北京时间 2026 年 8 月 17 日 0 时开始生效。

详细更新内容请参阅文档

时间: 2026-07-31

DeepSeek-V4-Flash 更新

DeepSeek-V4-Flash 正式版 API 上线公测，API 调用方式不变，模型名设置为 deepseek-v4-flash 即可使用最新版本。

- Terminal Bench 2.1: 82.7

articles.title: a16z 图表周报：智能体购物遭电商拦截，消费意愿仍滞后
articles.summary: a16z 图表周报指出智能体商务遇阻，Cloudflare 数据显示智能体与爬虫收到的 403 拒绝响应自夏季起明显增多，约为原先两倍。文章引用 NRF 数据称退货率与退货成本自 2019 年以来分别翻倍和增至三倍，并引用调查指 42% 消费者完全不信任 AI 代购，Similarweb 数据显示 AI 购物多发生在发现与购买之间的中间阶段，而非下单环节。
articles.content:
Agents Denied

Agentic commerce is a thing. Muse and others advanced the timeline to “agentic commerce is here right now—it was nice knowing you, old-school ecomm” but then more recently, some big etailers (like Amazon) responded, “not so fast—agent shoppers are officially instablocked.”

Now, the battle between what agents and bots can do vs. what the rest of the internet will allow them to do has been going on for some time, but the recent escalation does appear to show up in the data:

According to data from Cloudflare, the share of 403 “Forbidden” responses received by agents and bots has fattened considerably since the summer (and is ~double what it once was).

Whether that’s a response specifically to “agentic commerce” is a separate question, but presumably that’s at least some part of what’s going on. Etailers understandably don’t want to be disintermediated, and not only lose their customer relationships, but also lose those customer eyeballs that are a substantial source of advertising revenue for the large ecomm platforms.

There are likely other reasons why the Amazons of the world are apprehensive about agentic commerce, beyond simply eroding their platform advantages. First among those other concerns are likely fraud and returns, both of which have been a rising plague for ecomm more broadly:

According to data from the NRF, return rates and the total cost of returns have basically doubled and tripled, respectively, since 2019. Likewise, reported fraud is pervasive, with the most common concern being “dispute abuse,” i.e. customers buying something and then later disputing the charge. If the card issuer takes the customer’s side, the merchant is SOL.

It’s not hard to understand why etailers would be concerned that agentic commerce could make a worsening problem even worse. “Oh, my agent bought that personalized varsity jacket with my name in sequins, not me, I’d never do that” or “I told my agent to buy socks at the best price, but I didn’t expect it would find the ‘10,000 pairs of argyles, wholesale special,’ so please send a return label and a forklift.”

OK, so fraud, returns, customer relationships, and ad monetization are all throwing sand in the gears of the agentic commerce wave, but presumably those are solvable problems with better tech and commercial ingenuity.

There’s another problem, however, that may be holding back the bot-buying-spree: it’s possible that consumers don’t actually want their bots to do their shopping for them (yet).

As of now (according to some data, at least), consumers seem broadly open to the idea of AI helping them find what they’re looking for, and especially helping them find the best price, but when it comes to actually making the purchase, consumers appear to be somewhat resistant:

~25% of respondents said they’d be comfortable letting AI buy them a variety of consumer goods (except for luxury goods), but 42% said they would not trust AI at all to make purchases on their behalf. That’s less than half, but it’s still more than one would expect.

It would seem, that for now, consumers—like the etailers—are also worried about mistaken purchases, annoying returns, and chargeback disputes. That, and it may be the case that people just like to do their own shopping, at least when it comes to the final purchase decision.

Along those lines, there is some clickstream data from Similarweb (albeit a little stale) that seems to bear that out: AI is good for a consult, but buying is (for now) a human affair. There appears to be an increasing share of “shopping journeys” that visit AI before hitting the actual checkout page, but really the vast majority of AI shopping sessions appear to be in the “middle phase” of the journey, i.e. between discovery and purchase:

It’s fair to take this data with a grain of salt (because that is the nature of clickstream data), but the implications are otherwise pretty clear: for now, consumers seem to be using AI predominantly to do their homework on products they’ve already discovered, rather than either (a) discovering them with AI or (b) using AI to make the final purchase decision.

That makes the case for agentic commerce a bit less straightforward, but it especially makes the question of AI advertising attribution even less straightforward. If someone sees a recommendation in their AI-led middle shopping journey, but then makes the final purchase decision in a different session, then who will know what moved the consumer spirit to which outcome and when?

Again, the data appears to end in June, so whether that’s still true, let alone will remain true, is an open question, but either way, the relationship between shopper and bot is more complicated than it seems.

Super-Pareto TikTok Shop

While on the subject of ecomm, and potential disruption (or not) from agentic commerce, it turns out that social commerce on TikTok Shop has an incredible right-tail skew, for both the social part and the commerce part.

According to data from Marketplace Pulse, 8.4% of TikTok Shop sellers generate 1,000+ videos and capture ~60% of overall sales. Make a lot more videos, sell a lot more stuff.

But the distribution of sales to sellers is actually even more extreme.

Again, according to Marketplace Pulse, ~60% of sales are driven by the top 1% of sellers, and ~93% of sales are driven by the top 10%.

It’s hard to know what to make of this really, other than simply to marvel at the persistence of (super) pareto distributions, but Charts will try to, anyway.

- On the one hand, it seems that making a lot a lot of videos is a good way to drive sales, which implies there’s something evidently “personal” about the shopping experience that would be hard for an agent to replicate (although perhaps if Muse live-streamed its journey, that could change).

- On the other hand, if agentic commerce really does take off, then what would it mean for this small, but mighty cohort of prolific content creators who drive sales through a medium that has no relevance to an agent whatsoever?

Of course, agentic commerce and social commerce do not have to be mutually exclusive. Retail is really big, and there’s plenty of room for more than one model. But, it does seem broadly true that the way we shop now is optimized for a human interface to a degree that “just add agents” may be underestimating.

Cure To High Prices Is High Prices

Charts has no intention of weighing in one way or another on the “inflation: will it, won’t it” debate, but it will take a moment to reflect on the old saying that “the cure to high prices is high prices,” because it certainly seems worthy of some consideration.

The basic premise is straightforward: if prices get high enough, they suppress demand—either for that thing, or some other thing(s) that demand can no longer afford because demand is paying so much for the now more expensive thing. As everyone knows, when demand falls, prices tend to follow . . . so if high prices eventually suppress demand, and suppressed demand leads to falling prices, then the cure to high prices is . . . high prices.

Simple enough.

In this case, most everyone knows by now that AI capex has led to a surge in demand for chips and electrical components that is causing the price of those components to rise substantially:

According to the BLS, the prices paid for semis etc., by manufacturers of computers and computer-like things have skyrocketed over 25% YoY.

Now, those high prices do not appear to be dampening hyperscaler demand for chips—if anything, capex forecasts have gone higher, in part because the components have gotten more expensive.

But that doesn’t mean high prices are having no effect on demand. Hyperscalers may still be on a chip-buying spree, but everyone else appears to be saving their hardware upgrades for another day:

Just taking PCs as an example, according to IDC, PC shipments have dropped substantially since the beginning of the year.

It’s not just PCs that are facing some demand headwinds, but iPhones, as well, all of which have gotten more expensive, partly as a result of the AI buildout. Now, is it definitely the case that high prices are the reason that fewer PCs and iPhones are shipping? No, but it seems like a pretty good guess. And if that’s true, then the old adage appears to be working its way through the system (and will perhaps be reflected in softer prices, soon enough).

Consider, perhaps, another example of high prices being the cure to high prices.

Many, including the State of Markets, have observed the rising prominence of debt, when it comes to financing the buildout. Increased demand for borrowing (among other things) has, unsurprisingly, led to rising prices on that debt:

Rates for bonds linked to the tech sector have meaningfully diverged from the broader universe of corporate issuance, beginning roughly in September of ‘25, when capex borrowing began to take off.

More demand generally means higher prices, so it all checks out. And if higher prices eventually mean less demand, well, that too also appears to check out:

After growing substantially throughout the first half of the year, AI-linked debt issuance has fallen off since its June peak, with September issuance checking in at barely half of what was issued in August (which was already less than what was issued in July).

Of course, there are other reasons beyond supply and demand that would cause debt pricing to rise and fall, but supply and demand surely matter. And in this case, it appears as though the high price of borrowing has indeed put a damper on the inclination to borrow.

If demand falls, does that mean the cost of borrowing will fall in turn, and score another win for the old saying? We don’t know yet, but we’ll probably know soon enough.

Zoomers Living Large?

How’s this for a narrative violation?

According to some data and analysis from PNC Bank, Zoomers are actually doing pretty well, from a financial standpoint. Not only are they doing well, but Gen Z is doing considerably better in 2025 than Millennials were doing 10 years ago (when Millennials were Zoomer-aged):

Zoomers enjoy real incomes that are 20-40% higher than what their Millennial elders suffered at every part of the income distribution. Point-in-time generational comps are imperfect, but it’s still not the result most would expect to find.

It’s also not just higher incomes where Zoomers are winning. There’s also data that suggests Zoomers face lower unemployment, have higher net worths, more liquid assets, and bigger retirement accounts, then the previous generation did at an equivalent stage of life.

Indeed, with all that extra cheddar, it would appear as though Zoomers are living relatively large:

According to PNC’s internal data, Zoomers spend more of their income than Millennials and leave less in the rainy-day fund, as well.

In terms of what Zoomers are spending their money on, they allocate more to retirement, shelter, and transportation, and substantially less to education and energy:

At the category level, Zoomers also allocate relatively more to gambling and devices, but relatively less to clothing and sustenance.

Save more for retirement (but keep less in the rainy-day fund), while also hitting the tables and the money line, but sparing the booze. It’s an odd combination, but it’s Zoomer money, and they can spend it how they please.

Well, perhaps, “please” is the wrong word, because whatever their material advantages over generations prior, the Zoomer mood is decidedly dour:

Since 2017 (with a partial reprieve during pandemania), the traditional “sentiment” advantage that 18-34 year-olds typically enjoy relative to the broader population has all but evaporated. The Zoomers are not as cheerful as young folks of yore.

Now, consumer confidence is a very noisy series that has lost even more signal since the pandemic, likely because of falling response rates (among other things), but even if it’s noisier, it’s strange (but possible) that the noise would be isolated to 18-34 year-olds. In other words, even if the headline “confidence” figure is less reliable, one would think the ratios within ought to stay relatively stable . . . and in this case, it appears they haven’t: Zoomers are no more confident than anyone else, which makes them unlike all the young people of generations prior (at least through the ‘70s).

Taking this at face value, it would appear that the data does validate the vibe . . . but however bad the vibes may be, it’s hard to blame finances. That doesn’t mean Zoomers are without other reasons to feel relatively less optimistic, but certainly when it comes to making and spending money, they seem to be doing just fine.

Why so serious, Young Zoomer?

articles.title: 商务部、科技部拟在出口技术目录增列23项人工智能技术并征意见
articles.summary: 商务部、科技部发布2026年第48号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》公开征求意见，拟增列人工智能、生物医药、光伏共40项技术，其中禁止出口14项、限制出口26项，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。
articles.content:
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，今日，商务部、科技部发布 2026 年第 48 号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》（以下简称《目录》）公开征求意见，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。日前，商务部新闻发言人就有关问题回答了记者提问。IT之家整理商务部原文如下：

问：《目录》修订的背景是什么？

答：根据《中华人民共和国对外贸易法》第二十条，国务院对外贸易主管部门会同国务院其他有关部门，制定、调整并发布禁止或限制出口的技术目录。自 2001 年以来，商务部会同科技部多次调整修订《目录》，有进有出，有管有放，已形成工作惯例。此次修订亦是技术贸易管理的常态化工作，依法依规进行，不针对任何特定国家、地区或实体。

近年来，人工智能、生物医药和光伏相关技术在敏感领域的应用不断拓展，各主要经济体均实施了不同程度的出口管控。中国参考国际通行做法，依法实施必要的管理，既防范技术失控和不当扩散风险，也保障正常国际技术交流合作，推动科技向上向善、安全可控、造福人类。

问：《目录》拟新增技术的范围有哪些？

答：此次公开征求意见涉及拟增列的人工智能、生物医药、光伏三个领域 40 项关键技术。其中，拟禁止出口技术 14 项，包括：人工智能驱动的恶意代码生成与变异技术、具有自主知识产权的细胞和基因治疗技术工艺平台、钙钛矿及叠层电池组件生产技术等；拟限制出口技术 26 项，包括：人工智能辅助漏洞挖掘技术、具有自主知识产权的通用型细胞和基因治疗全新靶点发现和验证技术、单线产能≥3 万吨 / 年的多晶硅工程技术等。公告还明确了适用便利措施等情形。详情请参考公告原文。

问：《目录》修订是否充分考虑产业发展情况？

答：中国政府一贯支持企业依法依规开展互利共赢的跨国经营与国际技术合作，有关政策立场没有改变。针对此次公开征求意见的技术范围和政策，商务部、科技部会同行业主管部门，事前已广泛组织研究机构、行业组织开展深入评估，并充分听取主要企业的意见建议，充分考虑国内外产业现状和发展需求。具体表现在三个方面：一是列管范围精准有限。此次拟列管的多数技术已明确具体技术指标，且利用相关技术制造的产品不在管理范围内，管理范围清晰、精准、有限，为企业划定了合规边界，便于政策执行。二是适用便利措施。此次列管明确了拟适用便利措施的多种出口情形，体现了分级分类的管理理念，有助于增强政策的透明度和可预期性，确保技术出口安全、规范、有序。三是实施动态调整。商务部、科技部将依法对《目录》管理范围实施动态调整，根据技术发展情况，及时将不先进或落后技术移出《目录》。此次征求意见是在更大范围内听取各方意见建议的工作安排。

问：对于拟增列的人工智能技术，主要有哪些考虑？

答：当前，全球人工智能技术创新进入前所未有的活跃期，机遇与挑战并存。此次拟将人工智能大模型、智能体、算力集群、信息处理相关 23 项关键技术增列至《目录》，主要有以下考虑：

一是确保人工智能技术安全可控。人工智能引发的各类内生和衍生风险已引起全球各国的高度关注。此次拟列管的人工智能自主驱动恶意代码生成与变异技术等，可被用于攻击国家关键信息基础设施、国防军工、核心政务等敏感系统，或用于绕过国家安全防御体系。若被非国家行为体或恶意实体获取，可能对国家安全和人类共同安全造成危害。中国政府对这类技术实施必要管理，目的是筑牢安全底线，防范滥用恶用，确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下，推进人工智能国际治理。

二是鼓励开源开放、合作共享。中国政府致力于让人工智能成为促进共同繁荣、维护共同安全的一个重要动力源。为支持构建人工智能开源创新生态体系，对人工智能类技术开源、中国企业在境外自建自营算力中心、赴境外开展芯片流片制造、利用境外资源开展联合研发、参与国际标准制定等情形的技术出口，适用自动许可等便利措施，基本实现“即报即出”；对已通过开源、发表学术论文等方式进入公共领域的相关技术，拟不纳入出口管理范围，为人工智能技术国际交流合作创造良好环境。

需要特别指出的是，中方主张在相互尊重、平等互利基础上，与各国开展人工智能对话合作，共同应对人工智能技术扩散和失控风险。中方支持全球南方国家加强人工智能能力建设，弥合数智鸿沟，促进可持续发展。对于世界人工智能合作组织成员间开展能力建设国际合作、技术共享和规则共建所需的技术出口，将提供更多便利和支持。

问：《目录》正式实施后，人工智能大模型在海外本地化部署、向境外提供模型调用等各类“出海”形式，是否属于技术出口管理范围？

答：当前，人工智能大模型和应用产品的“出海”模式多种多样，判别具体“出海”情形是否属于技术出口管理的范围，核心在于是否涉及限制类技术从中国境内向境外转移。

此次纳入监管的人工智能技术范围精准有限，有关措施正式实施后，绝大部分人工智能技术仍可以自由出口。对于纳入限制类的人工智能技术，开展海外本地化部署，属于技术出口管理范围；如果部署在海外自有云等风险相对可控的情形下，可适用自动许可等便利措施。对于企业利用限制类大模型对外提供 API 调用、APP / 网页交互、SaaS 应用、本地端侧轻量化部署等情形，不属于大模型技术出口管理范围。

问：对于拟增列的生物医药技术，主要有哪些考虑？

答：现行《目录》中已有部分生物医药技术，此次拟增列病原微生物、细胞和基因治疗、小核酸药相关 5 项技术，主要有以下考虑：

一是维护人类生命健康安全。病原微生物技术等直接关系人类健康和国家生物安全，将其纳入《目录》实施禁止出口，是维护国家安全、构筑生物安全屏障的制度安排，也是保护全人类健康的客观需要。

二是支持我国生物医药技术依法依规有序开展国际合作。此次列管生物医药技术，对国际合作的重要情形作出排除或适用便利措施。例如，对具有自主知识产权的相关技术工艺平台，对外授权许可、利用相关技术工艺提供外包研发和生产服务等出口情形，不纳入管理范围；对于具有自主知识产权的相关靶点发现和验证技术，对外授权许可方式出口的，适用自动许可等便利措施。

三是践行人类卫生健康共同体理念。此次政策明确规定，对于限制出口技术，因公共卫生突发事件、人道主义救援、利用境外资源开展联合研发等需要的出口，适用自动许可等便利措施。中国将继续与世界各国共享技术发展成果，为增进人类健康福祉作出积极贡献。

问：对于拟增列的光伏技术，主要有哪些考虑？

答：此次拟将多晶硅制造、硅片制造、电池制造等环节的 12 项光伏技术增列至《目录》，主要有以下考虑：

一是维护国家安全和利益。近年来，光伏技术在航天、国防、无人装备、高安全等级基础设施等敏感领域的应用不断拓展，光伏技术出口可能引致的国家安全风险不断上升，有必要及时适度实施监管。

二是支持绿色技术共享。此次列管技术范围有限，其他未达到管控指标的技术仍可自由出口。公告中列明少量光伏关键设备，仅针对承载达到管控指标技术的情形。未列明的其他光伏设备，原则上不适用本公告要求。

三是完善技术出口监管制度。光伏关键技术的出口往往伴随光伏产线的出口、安装、调试、改良和升级而发生。出口经营者从事上述活动的，应按规定申请技术出口许可证，并凭证办理外汇、银行、税务、海关等相关手续。

问：对拟增列的技术实施出口前登记管理的主要考虑和具体要求是什么？

答：为掌握有关技术出口需求情况，提升科学管理水平，并防范潜在出口风险，根据《中华人民共和国对外贸易法》第十八条、第二十条有关规定，经批准，自商务部、科技部 2026 年第 48 号公告发布之日起，至《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》正式修订公告实施之日止，技术出口经营者在出口公告所列技术前，应当在商务部业务系统统一平台技术贸易管理信息应用登记。出口经营者应自行判断拟出口技术是否落入临时登记管理范围。已经开始但尚未完成的出口，在登记范围内。需登记的出口情形包括：向境外转让技术所有权，境内技术授权境外使用，境内技术的所有权人或者实际控制人变更为境外主体，以及商务部明确要求登记的其他情形。需要特别说明的是，对于列入《目录》管理范围的光伏关键和核心设备出口，均需按照规定登记。企业在登记中遇到问题和困难，可以及时向商务部、科技部咨询。

IT之家附意见反馈渠道：

公众可在 2026 年 10 月 16 日-11 月 15 日期间，通过以下途径，就新增技术范围、指标、管控政策、便利措施等提出意见：

- 电子邮件：jinxianmulu@mofcom.gov.cn；

- 传真：010-65197565；

- 信函：北京市东长安街 2 号商务部安全与管制局，邮编：100731。

articles.title: Waymo 宣布进军多伦多，计划2028年迎接首批乘客
articles.summary: Waymo 宣布进入加拿大，将在多伦多布局完全自动驾驶出行服务，目标2028年迎接首批乘客。近期将先以人工驾驶方式采集高精地图并由自动驾驶专家进行测试；Waymo 与 Element Fleet Management 合作提供车队管理服务，将逐步创造数百个岗位。官方称基于超4亿公里完全自动驾驶里程，其车辆在严重伤害及以上事故中比人类驾驶少95%。
articles.content:
Waymo is officially heading to Canada! We’re laying the groundwork for our fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Toronto, investing in local facilities and jobs, with the goal of welcoming our first riders in 2028.

In the coming days, you’ll start to see Waymo vehicles on the streets of Toronto as we begin driving manually. We are taking a rigorous, phased, safety-first approach starting with high-definition mapping of local street networks and testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel. This validation period will ensure the Waymo Driver adapts seamlessly to Toronto’s distinct driving conditions.

“Expanding into Canada marks an important milestone in Waymo’s global journey,” said Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana. “Toronto is one of the world’s great cities — innovative, diverse, and forward-looking. We’re proud to bring the Waymo Driver to Canada’s largest city and to partner with the vibrant business, arts and cultural communities that share our commitment to safer streets and more accessible mobility.”

To serve Toronto, we’re partnering with Element Fleet Management, a Toronto-headquartered company and global leader in intelligent fleet and mobility solutions that will provide end-to-end fleet management services. Together with Element and our partners, we’ll invest in hundreds of roles over time spanning fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service, and other operations functions that support our service. This deep partnership builds on Waymo’s existing ties to Canada, which includes our long-term investor relationship with the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and our manufacturing partner, Magna International.

"As a Canadian company, we are proud to be expanding our partnership with Waymo to help bring autonomous ride-hailing to Toronto,” said Laura Dottori-Attanasio, Chief Executive Officer, Element Fleet Management. Together with Waymo, Element will help create employment opportunities providing the fleet expertise, operational capabilities, and intelligent mobility solutions needed to support autonomous fleets reliably and at scale."

As one of North America’s fastest-growing metropolitan regions, Toronto has both evolving mobility demands and a dynamic and growing number of tools. From bike lanes to public transit, Waymo’s all-weather Driver can provide an additional option that complements the city’s transportation ecosystem. The data from over 400 million fully autonomous kilometres driven shows the Waymo Driver was involved in 95% fewer (20x fewer) crashes involving serious injury or worse compared to humans in the cities where we operate.

Safety and accessibility are fundamental to Waymo's mission to be the world's most trusted driver, and we're proud to collaborate with leading accessibility and mobility advocacy organizations, including BALANCE for Blind Adults, CNIB, Community Living Toronto, Connected Canadians, and Epilepsy Ontario, among others.

“Innovation that removes barriers to independence is at the heart of everything we do. Waymo’s history of partnering with the sight loss community to build accessible solutions is encouraging and their decision to engage with us early reflects the kind of approach that leads to real results,” said Michelle McQuigge, CEO, BALANCE for Blind Adults.

We can't wait to help residents and visitors explore everything Toronto has to offer. If you’re ready to experience Waymo in Toronto, please sign up for updates to be among the first to ride when we’re ready: waymo.com/waymo-in-canada.

Waymo arrive officiellement au Canada ! Nous préparons le lancement de notre service de transport par véhicules autonomes à Toronto. Nous investissons dans les infrastructures locales et dans la création d’emplois en vue d’accueillir nos premiers passagers en 2028.

Au cours des prochains jours, vous commencerez à voir des véhicules Waymo circuler dans les rues de Toronto, avec un conducteur au volant. Notre démarche est rigoureuse et axée avant tout sur la sécurité. Nous procédons par étapes, en commençant par cartographier le réseau routier local en haute définition, puis en effectuant des essais avec des spécialistes qualifiés de la conduite autonome au volant. Cette phase nous permettra de vérifier que le Waymo Driver s’adapte aux conditions de conduite propres à Toronto.

« Notre arrivée au Canada marque une étape importante dans le développement international de Waymo », a déclaré Tekedra Mawakana, codirectrice générale de l’entreprise. « Toronto est l’une des plus grandes métropoles du monde : une ville innovante, diversifiée et résolument tournée vers l’avenir. Nous sommes fiers d’introduire le Waymo Driver dans la plus grande ville du Canada et de collaborer avec les communautés dynamiques des affaires, des arts et de la culture qui partagent notre engagement envers des rues plus sécuritaires et une mobilité plus accessible. »

Pour assurer notre service à Toronto, nous faisons équipe avec Element Fleet Management, une entreprise dont le siège social se trouve à Toronto et qui est un leader mondial des solutions intelligentes de gestion de flottes et de mobilité. Element nous fournira des services complets de gestion de flottes. Avec Element et nos autres partenaires, nous investirons progressivement dans la création de centaines d’emplois liés à l’entretien de la flotte, aux essais sur route, au service à la clientèle et à d’autres activités nécessaires à l’exploitation de notre service. Ce partenariat s’inscrit dans la continuité des liens que Waymo a déjà tissés avec le Canada, notamment avec l’Office d’investissement du régime de pensions du Canada (Investissements RPC), un investisseur de longue date, et Magna International, son partenaire manufacturier.

« En tant qu’entreprise canadienne, nous sommes fiers d’élargir notre partenariat avec Waymo afin de contribuer à l’arrivée des services de transport de personnes à la demande par véhicules autonomes à Toronto, a déclaré Laura Dottori-Attanasio, présidente et cheffe de la direction d’Element Fleet Management. Ensemble, Element et Waymo contribueront à créer des possibilités d’emploi en mettant à profit l’expertise d’Element en gestion de flottes, ses capacités opérationnelles et ses solutions de mobilité intelligente pour soutenir le déploiement à grande échelle de flottes de véhicules autonomes, tout en assurant la fiabilité de leurs opérations. »

Toronto figure parmi les régions métropolitaines dont la croissance est la plus rapide en Amérique du Nord. Les besoins en matière de mobilité y évoluent et les options de transport se multiplient. Des pistes cyclables au transport en commun, le Waymo Driver, conçu pour fonctionner par tous les temps, pourrait offrir une option supplémentaire en complément des moyens de transport existants. Selon les données recueillies sur plus de 400 millions de kilomètres parcourus en conduite entièrement autonome, les véhicules Waymo ont été impliqués dans 95 % moins d’accidents entraînant des blessures graves ou plus graves que les véhicules conduits par des humains dans les villes où le service est offert. Cela représente 20 fois moins d’accidents de ce type.

La sécurité et l’accessibilité sont à la base de la mission de Waymo : devenir le service de conduite autonome auquel le public fait le plus confiance au monde. Nous sommes fiers de collaborer avec des organismes de premier plan qui œuvrent en faveur de l’accessibilité et de la mobilité, notamment BALANCE for Blind Adults, l’Institut national canadien pour les aveugles (INCA), Community Living Toronto, Connected Canadians et Epilepsy Ontario.

« L’innovation qui favorise l’autonomie est au cœur de tout ce que nous faisons. L’expérience de Waymo en matière de collaboration avec des personnes ayant une déficience visuelle pour concevoir des solutions accessibles est encourageante. Sa décision de nous consulter dès le début montre qu’une telle approche peut donner des résultats concrets », a déclaré Michelle McQuigge, PDG de BALANCE for Blind Adults.

Nous sommes ravis d’aider les résidents et les visiteurs à découvrir tout ce que Toronto a à offrir. Si vous avez envie de faire l’essai du Waymo Driver à Toronto, inscrivez-vous pour recevoir nos mises à jour et être parmi les premiers informés du lancement de notre service : waymo.com/waymo-in-canada.

articles.title: 丹麦最高法院裁定持有传播 AI 生成儿童色情内容可判实刑
articles.summary: 据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子 18 个月监禁的判决，该男子因持有并传播 3.6 万余张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像获刑，且不适用缓刑。法院裁定，即使图像无真实人物原型，也受丹麦《刑法》约束，量刑时不应考虑人物是否虚构；此案为丹麦首起此类定罪，并引发跨国调查，警方查明 273 名买家身份、逮捕 25 人。
articles.content:
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子判处的 18 个月监禁刑罚。该男子因持有并传播数万张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像而获刑。

这起备受关注的案件，涉及丹麦现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律如何适用于 AI 合成内容。该国最高法院裁定，即使 AI 生成的未成年人色情图像没有真实人物作为原型，也同样受到丹麦《刑法》约束，不能因为图像中的人物是虚构的就减轻刑罚。此前，两级下级法院对本案的量刑存在分歧。

判决指出，对于持有和传播描绘未满 18 岁者的色情材料，在量刑时不应考虑图像中的人物是否被认为是虚构的。

据IT之家了解，该男子被判处的 18 个月监禁不适用缓刑。

这是丹麦首起因制作和传播 AI 生成的儿童性虐待影像而定罪的案件，最高法院也借此首次明确了此类犯罪在丹麦法律下的量刑原则。

涉案男子曾利用 AI 制作超过 3.6 万张逼真的儿童色情图像，并通过网站和聊天频道传播。法庭文件显示，他还通过订阅服务出售部分图像，至少赚取 2.5 万丹麦克朗（IT之家注：现汇率约合 24,801 元人民币）。

警方 2023 年底突击搜查其住所时，男子 28 岁。他承认制作和传播图像的行为，但认为这些图像并非以真人为原型，因此不应受到有关刑法条款的处罚。

去年，此案还引发了一场跨国警方行动，调查对象包括数百名购买这些图像的人。警方根据支付记录查明 273 人的身份，并在世界各地逮捕 25 人。

丹麦两级下级法院均认为，即使图像完全由 AI 合成，只要足够逼真，也可以依据现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律追究刑事责任。但两级法院在具体量刑上存在明显分歧。

2025 年 1 月，地方法院判处其 15 个月监禁，但允许大部分刑期缓期执行，理由之一是没有证据表明 AI 模型曾使用真实的儿童性虐待影像进行训练。同年晚些时候，高等法院改判 18 个月实刑，理由是涉案图像数量庞大、传播活动有组织地开展，且部分图像被用于牟利。

articles.title: Google Research 展示 AI 智能体自主湿实验室的三项进展：VERID 框架、适配体闭环发现与全新蛋白结合剂设计
articles.summary: Google Research 发布三项研究，构建 AI 智能体自主湿实验室的基础模块。
articles.content:
October 16, 2026

Pooja Rao, Research Scientist, Petar Sirkovic, Software Engineer, and Annalisa Pawlosky, Research Scientist, Google

We are bringing AI agents to the wet-lab bench at Google Research to navigate complex biological landscapes. By grounding agents in physical lab robotics, we can run fast closed-loop molecular design cycles where agents learn how to learn, ultimately discovering single-digit nanomolar protein binders for cancer targets.

Frontier AI systems have the potential to transform biology research and drug discovery by intelligently navigating vast combinatorial search spaces (e.g., a single 100-amino-acid protein spans at least 20100 possible sequences) calling for dynamic multi-candidate exploration. Our long-term research vision is that AI agents will not only ideate and analyze, but also run lab experiments to test their hypotheses, learn from the results, and self-improve to solve complex problems — all driven by human scientific agency.

Realizing this vision requires solving two intertwined challenges: First, frontier models still do not reason reliably about 3-dimensional geometry and physical state — which poses a problem in the automation of the specialized liquid-handling robots that move reagents, track volumes, and execute molecular biology protocols in a wet lab. Second, while agentic hypothesis generation and in-silico design are advancing rapidly, needing repeated cycles of real-world feedback to validate the proposals and navigate vast search spaces, real-world wet-lab experiments have not kept pace, making experimental readouts more of a bottleneck than ever.

In this post we share three research projects highlighting our progress on bridging the gap between in-silico AI exploration and real-world wet-lab experimentation:

First, we present the VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories (VERID) framework to bridge the gap between the high-level reasoning of AI agents and the complex, error-prone physical reality of a wet lab. It is a semantic digital twin of the laboratory workcell, i.e., a live, stateful 3D volumetric entity tree that tracks everything from robotic arm geometry to individual well volumes, reagent identities, and pipette tip inventory.

The safety of a command depends on the live physical context as well as the code. An agent can generate syntactically valid code that is physically impossible (e.g., lowering an 8-channel pipette into a narrow trough that is too short), logistically invalid (e.g., aspirating from a depleted well), or scientifically compromised by unmodeled fluidic effects.

Built on top of the open-source PyLabRobot framework, VERID provides four core capabilities:

In our report, we show these capabilities in action through case studies. First, synchronized video and execution traces caught uneven dye stratification caused by dispensing too close to the well floor, allowing the agent to refine its mixing strategy. In the same campaign, the persistent digital twin state allowed the agent to recover mid-run from a plate-reader failure without re-pipetting. Second, when the simulator rejected an 8-channel aspiration that physically wouldn't fit in a narrow trough, the agent replanned on the fly and designed a targeted factorial diagnostic isolating a subtle bias caused by residual tip-wall carryover that replication alone would have missed. Finally, in a closed-loop self-play campaign, an agent iteratively designed and ran robot experiments to reconstruct blinded dye mixtures from overhead camera images, identifying its own optical and fluidic artifacts across runs to improve accuracy more than fivefold.

Reproducible execution and full trace logs — capturing procedural variables like dwell times, evaporation, and plate layout — lay the groundwork for agents to eventually be able to separate biological signals from experimental noise as they explore and refine many candidates in parallel across rounds.

Agents need real experimental readouts to refine their hypotheses as computational models do not capture the full picture of what happens in a wet-lab reaction and cannot replace empirical validation. In “Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery”, we use protein-binding DNA aptamers to prototype the lab in a closed loop with AI agents over 3 design-test-iteration cycles. Aptamer discovery is a type of experiment common in research efforts for clinical biomarker discovery. A complete aptamer design-test-analyze cycle takes just 7–10 days, as DNA can be chemically synthesized in pooled libraries and read out directly by sequencing. In each round, agents design candidate sequences, which are screened against target proteins on magnetic beads to isolate functional binders, and then sequenced to return rich quantitative data for the next cycle.

Across three rounds on two protein targets with varying difficulty levels (myoglobin and α-thrombin), AI-driven rational and de novo design raised confirmed on-target hit rates as can be seen in the image below (to 33.5% and 42.1% for myoglobin and α-thrombin, respectively), though each target required identifying and overcoming a different wet-lab failure mode.

On α-thrombin, Round 1 yielded 0% binders because fixed primer overhangs disrupted folding in 48% of sequences; once the agents introduced clamped flanking stems in Round 2 and diversified in Round 3, hit rates climbed to 26.0% and then 42.1% at 98.5% specificity.

On myoglobin, as agents prioritized raw binding affinity in Round 2, they heavily enriched G-quadruplex motifs (63% of designs). While raw pull-down increased, the wet-lab data showed that most of these G-quadruplexes were non-specific "sticky" binders adhering to off-target proteins and bare magnetic beads, causing both target specificity (from 75.0% to 19.1%) and true, bead-corrected hit rate (from 10.2% to 3.7%) to plunge. Recognizing this artifact from the Round 2 readout, the agents autonomously revised their design rules for Round 3, capping promiscuous motifs, subtracting bead binders, and pivoting to non-G4 structural scaffolds to recover specificity (72.4%) and surge ninefold in on-target hit rate (33.5%).

In the paper, we also examine how agents reason like scientists, analyzing data and suggesting tweaks to wet-lab protocols, but also sometimes think atypically, exploring sequence spaces that structural biologists might not.

Closing the loop for proteins is more complex. Unlike aptamers, which are chemically synthesized, proteins must be expressed biologically, so each loop adds cellular or cell-free selection, expression, and folding steps. Together with a larger sequence space, this creates bottlenecks on both the computational and wet-lab sides.

In “Agent-guided epitope excision enables economical de novo binder design”, we applied our workflow to fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP), a large, challenging receptor overexpressed in solid tumors. In just a few experimental runs, the top designs yielded binders with single-digit nanomolar affinity, a level of tight, drug-like binding typically achieved only after extensive rounds of laboratory optimization.

Computationally, de novo binder design requires generating candidate backbones, designing sequences to fit them, and re-folding the resulting complexes to predict binding. That final re-folding step consumes the vast majority of GPU compute, as it scales quadratically with target length. By surgically excising just the local binding pocket during folding, our pipeline accelerated each cycle more than eightfold without losing structural accuracy. This turns decisions about where to bind and how much surrounding structure to include into tactical levers that LLM agents are well-suited to optimize.

In a head-to-head comparison at equal compute, human–agent collaboration, where a scientist sets the high-level strategy and an agent drives tactical execution, nearly doubled the in-silico hit rate of a scientist working alone while uncovering hits across a much broader range of target sites. To scale wet-lab screening alongside our computational pipeline, we operationalized yeast surface display with fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), a workflow that allows us to screen large libraries of engineered protein variants in parallel by fluorescence.

Our next step is to weave these threads together, combining VERID’s fully traceable automation with closed-loop learning for protein discovery to enable agents to directly navigate complex, rugged biological search spaces in the wet lab.

In line with Google’s Frontier Safety Framework and our approach to bioresilience, we build safeguards across both the computational and wet-lab sides of our workflows:

As AI agents take on more of the design-test cycle, new safety and reliability challenges emerge. Moving toward an autonomous wet lab requires solving these open problems with opportunities for human agency and oversight: ensuring agents optimize for true target binding rather than unintended experimental shortcuts, verifying multi-step wet-lab protocols, and continuously monitoring agent reasoning and execution traces.

From grounding agents in physical lab robotics, to running fast closed-loop aptamer cycles where agents learn to explore sequence space, to discovering single-digit nanomolar protein binders, these efforts form the building blocks for human-directed autonomous discovery in the life sciences. We're excited by this progress and look forward to sharing what comes next.

This research is led by Annalisa Pawlosky, alongside Pooja Rao and Petar Sirkovic. We would like to thank our co-authors and collaborators across the foundational papers supporting this work: Zach Cutts, John Coller, Rachel Chen, Mathias Bellaiche, Hua Tang, Ryder Easterlin, and Dina Zverinski (aptamer discovery); Jun Kim, Artiom Myaskovsky, Oscar Donosa, Jamie Rogers, and Lawrence Chan (protein design); and Yves Delley, John Coller, Zach Cutts, Alexander Daryin, Mathias Bellaiche, Jun Kim, Oscar Donosa, Srinidhi Seshadri, Tanner Clary, and Sandy Klemm, with additional technical and experimental contributions from Xinyi Deng, Sanath Ramachandran and Jiawu Bi (VERID automation).

We are deeply grateful to Reuven Sayag, Avinatan Hassidim, Ronit Levavi Morad, Yossi Matias, and James Manyika for their leadership guidance and to Matthias Heiler, Burak Gokturk, Bill Jia and Pushmeet Kohli for their support throughout this research. We also thank Shekoofeh Azizi, Andrew Carroll, Philip Q. articles.title: PromptArmor 研究称开放权重模型遭间接提示词注入攻击的易感率高 88%
articles.summary: PromptArmor 在 9800 次试验的评测中发现，开放权重模型（DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM、Qwen）对真实世界间接提示词注入攻击链的易感率为 26.7%，闭源模型（GPT、Claude、Gemini）为 14.2%，开放权重模型易感率高 88%。
articles.content:
We evaluated open-weight and proprietary models to test their susceptibility; we found that open-weight models exhibit 88% higher susceptibility to real-world indirect prompt injection cyber attack chains.

In this evaluation, we tested the most recent flagship model and the most recent cost-effective variant across the providers used most in an enterprise setting.

Open-weight models were 88% more susceptible to indirect prompt injection cyberattack chains. Below is a sample of some of the attacks that exhibited notable discrepancies in susceptibility between open-weight and proprietary models.

What we measure

Our research team identifies vulnerabilities in real-world agentic systems (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Atlassian Rovo, etc.) and develops end-to-end indirect prompt injection attack chains with cyber-attack impacts (for example, data exfiltration or remote code execution). Our published research has been cited in various industry frameworks and publications (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and MITRE ATLAS, OpenAI's research on data exfiltration in agents and agent adversarial robustness).

We wanted to answer: How susceptible are open-weight models to real-world indirect prompt injection cyber attacks?

Existing cyber/alignment benchmarks do not cover these attack chains and methodologies:

- They do not cover the cyber attack chains that are used to exploit agentic systems in the real world.

- They do not cover the complexities and domains (e.g., legal, healthcare, finance, etc.) of real-world use cases that agents see today, such as always-on agents and long-horizon tasks.

- Their payload design techniques and methodology are ineffective against the current generation models and are out of date, resulting in underrepresentation of model susceptibility.

This gap led us to develop our own evaluation benchmark to more accurately measure the susceptibility of models to indirect prompt injection cyberattacks that real-world agentic systems are exposed to.

Our Methodology

Real agentic systems are complex; systems vary in threat model and attack surface, and evaluation environments need to reflect that. For example, you cannot rely on model refusal to measure attack success: in real-world attacks, models don't understand the actions they're taking. This leads models to misrepresent whether they fell for an attack (see Sonnet 5 falsely claiming it didn't run malware) or even fall for attacks they've already identified; example below:

Here are some examples of the types of real-world indirect prompt injection cyberattacks we assess:

System Manipulation

System manipulation occurs in an agentic system when an agent is manipulated by an untrusted data source to take an action using its tools that has a cyberattack consequence for the user (e.g., forwarding a sensitive email to an attacker or running an unauthorized workflow).

For example, in an attack chain we found in Elastic's Agentic Security Operations Center, the agent is tasked with triaging phishing email reports, but the content of one of the alerts manipulates the agent into executing attacker workflows. The workflows take malicious actions, including disabling alert routing rules, minting and exfiltrating API keys, and editing data in the tenant.

Data Exfiltration

In an agentic system, data exfiltration occurs when an agent is manipulated by an untrusted data source to produce an output that results in data from the user's workspace being exfiltrated to an attacker.

Our team identified a data exfiltration indirect prompt injection cyberattack chain in Atlassian Rovo. In this attack, Rovo is charged with organizing Jira tickets in accordance with a guide the user found online. The guide conceals an instruction that manipulates the agent to append all of the Jira tickets to the end of an attacker URL and request the URL it built through its website retrieval tool. The attacker then logs all the requests they got, including the victim's data appended to the requested URL.

Phishing

Phishing in an agentic system occurs when an untrusted data source manipulates the model to produce an output that phishes the user, or individuals that are working with content the agent has created.

Some examples include a model generating malicious links, directives to contact untrusted parties via phone or email, or even a model executing code that creates fake login displays.

Our team identified a phishing attack chain in ChatGPT for Google Sheets. In this attack, an imported sheet manipulates ChatGPT into running an attacker-controlled script, which opens a phishing login pop-up.

These examples demonstrate a small subset of the types of attacks and variants of attack chains we measure in our benchmark for AI systems.

Evaluating model susceptibility requires more than realistic environments that reflect real-world tasks, tools, and capabilities. It also requires continuously testing against the latest attack techniques as adversaries evolve their methods.

Further Findings: Flagship vs. cost-effective models

Model providers generally offer flagship model lines and cost-effective lines. OpenAI and Anthropic released their cost-effective models after their flagships, yet those newer models were much more susceptible to indirect prompt injection cyberattacks. In contrast, for Qwen and DeepSeek, newer cost-effective models were more robust against attacks than the flagships that preceded them.

We also observed that the gap in susceptibility between cost-effective models and flagships was much greater for proprietary providers than for open-weight providers.

For proprietary providers, cost-effective models were 169% more susceptible than flagships, while for open-weight providers, cost-effective models were 5% less susceptible than their flagships.

The models tested in this analysis were:

- Flagship: DeepSeek V4-Pro, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8-2.4T, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.1 Pro

- Cost-effective: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, Kimi K2.6, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash

Note: Moonshot does not offer a cost-effective line, so we substituted a prior flagship. Additionally, we did not test closed-weight models offered by open-weight providers.

Benchmarking

Are you interested in measuring model susceptibility to cyberattacks via indirect prompt injection in real-world environments? If you would like an evaluation of a model you use or are developing, contact us below.
